sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT] The Petek tracker now shows 98.17% of ballots counted at 02:02 (5,132,045 valid votes, 11,777 polling stations, 1,203 localities), up from 98.01% (5,123,252 valid votes) at the 04:00 scan. Seat projection is UNCHANGED: Netanyahu bloc 53, Eisenkot-led Change bloc 48, Arab parties 19, nobody at 61. The Central Elections Committee announced early Thursday that double-envelope counting began at 01:00 a.m. (03:00 ); its partial official update at 01:51 a.m. also kept seats at 53-48-19 (Likud 26, Yashar 21). The tracker display does not distinguish whether the +8,793-vote increment is double-envelope or late ordinary ballots -- do not claim either. Final count expected Oct 30; official results Nov 4.
sections.what_verified: Petek tracker (CEC-sourced per tracker; no declared tier in the registry) for the new 98.17% figure; the frozen 53-48-19 split is consistent with the CEC partial official update carried by Israel National News (undeclared) and Times of Israel (T3) reporting of the same count stage. Single family for the NEW figure itself.
sections.what_disputed: Older count stages still circulating in search results (Haaretz 89.8%, Tribune/ANI 90%) are SUPERSEDED by 98.17% and must not be re-reported as current. Likud's fraud allegation against Arab parties (recorded Oct 28) is unproven; the CEC says every inquiry will be examined. The CEC's own '90.5% of votes counted' phrasing at 01:51 a.m. uses a different denominator than Petek's 98.17% of ballots -- report each figure with its source, never blended.
sections.why_matters: Count advances, deadlock frozen: 98.17% in and still nobody at 61 -- the double-envelope ballots are the last lever, and the Arab-party kingmaker question is the fight.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE to totw-20261029-0400-01 (Israel election) -- Petek count advances 98.01% -> 98.17% at 02:02 Oct 29 (tracker time = 04:02 on the tracker's Israel-time convention, in-window); seats FROZEN at 53-48-19; valid votes 5,132,045 (+8,793)

totw_analysis: Our read: Count advances, deadlock frozen: 98.17% in and still nobody at 61 -- the double-envelope ballots are the last lever, and the Arab-party kingmaker question is the fight. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Should Eisenkot govern with Arab-party support from outside the coalition, or does that hand Netanyahu's camp its 'stolen election' charge?
